claim: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B total / ~13B active, FP4 routed experts, mostly FP8 non-expert weights) was served on eight MI250 GCDs of ~64 GiB HBM each as a single TP8/EP1 instance with no routed-expert all-to-all — i.e. the accepted topology avoids expert all-to-all entirely and puts everything on tensor parallelism.
stance_target: the repo's claim that EP's all-to-all is the thing to avoid on a slow fabric, and that TP-with-no-EP is the topology a serving stack picks when it wants to dodge it
scope_conditions: 8x MI250 GCDs (gfx90a/CDNA2), ~64 GiB HBM per GCD, SGLang, DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoint (48 safetensors shards)
quoted_support: Runtime topology: One TP8/EP1 instance, no routed-expert A2A; native decode graph tiers 1/2/4/8/16/32/64. ... DeepSeek-V4-Flash; 284B total parameters, approximately 13B active parameters, FP4 routed experts, and mostly FP8 non-expert weights.

claim: Single-request resident decode on that 8-GCD TP8 instance reaches 88.63 output tok/s, rising to 1,041.78 at concurrency 32 and 1,327.10 at concurrency 64 — a 284B MoE is servable across eight 64 GB cards.
stance_target: what a 284B-class MoE costs to serve on 8x64 GB, as a reference point for the 5x64 GB box
scope_conditions: Native autoregressive campaign, public-source code requests, three measured rounds per group, resident decode excludes admission and drain
quoted_support: Single-request resident decode reaches 88.63 output tokens/s, while C32 and C64 reach 1041.78 and 1327.10.

claim: Prefill at 32K input tokens reaches 9,966.84 input tok/s at concurrency 16 (10,263.02 at 16K, 10,413.87 at ~8K) — long-context prefill of a CSA-family MoE degrades only modestly from 8K to 32K on this stack.
stance_target: whether CSA-style compressed attention imposes a large prefill penalty at 32k, as the repo's 'CSA2 at 32k' question assumes
scope_conditions: C16 prefill, ~8K/16K/32K input length, accepted prefill configuration (reduced indexer replication, mHC reuse, paired-GCD attention, fixed-order expert reduction)
quoted_support: Separate C16 prefill measurements reach 10413.87, 10263.02, and 9966.84 input tokens/s at approximately 8K, 16K, and 32K input length.

claim: The accepted prefill configuration depends on reducing indexer replication across devices — i.e. the CSA indexer is expensive enough that duplicating it per tensor-parallel rank was a measurable cost, and cutting that replication was part of the winning config.
stance_target: the repo's claim that CSA2's indexer is a real compute cost that must be paid at training time too
scope_conditions: TP8 serving of DeepSeek-V4-Flash on MI250; accepted prefill configuration
quoted_support: The accepted prefill configuration combines reduced indexer replication, mHC reuse, paired-GCD attention, and fixed-order expert reduction.

claim: The KV pool is allocated at 1,048,576 logical tokens but the report explicitly certifies no filled-1M-context performance or quality, so 1M-context claims for this stack are occupancy, not measured behaviour.
stance_target: how much weight the 1M-token KV allocation can carry as evidence of long-context capability
scope_conditions: Table 1 evidence-backed state as of September 18, 2026
quoted_support: KV pool: 1,048,576 logical tokens allocated; no filled-1M-context performance or quality certification.

claim: The report separates component equality and bounded semantic checks from numerical equivalence, and lists dynamic batching, cold-shape compilation and untested million-token occupancy as explicit limitations — a model of the evidence discipline this run should apply to its own measurements.
stance_target: the evidence-tier discipline the repo's measured/reported/estimate labelling is trying to enforce
quoted_support: Component equality and bounded semantic checks do not establish universal numerical equivalence; dynamic batching, cold-shape compilation, and untested million-token occupancy remain explicit limitations.

claim: The study covers DeepSeek-V4 only and explicitly excludes V4.1 and Engram offload results, so it cannot be used to support claims about CSA2 or Engram memory behaviour.
stance_target: the boundary of what this source can be cited for in the CSA2/Engram parts of the query
quoted_support: This study does not include V4.1 or Engram offload results.
